questions.text:
Consider the following two-process synchronization solution.


The shared variable turn is initialized to zero.Which one of the following is TRUE?
questions.solution:
This is strict alternation: the processes must take turns. Mutual exclusion holds, but if process 0 wants to enter twice while process 1 does not want to enter at all, process 0 is blocked (turn = 1) by a process that is not even trying. That violates progress.

Answer: This solution violates progress requirement

questions.text:
Consider the following processes, with the arrival time and the length of the CPU burst given in milli seconds.The scheduling algorithm used is preemptive shortest remaining-time first.

The average turn around time of these processes is milliseconds.
questions.solution:
SRTF: P1 0-3 (7 left); P2 arrives (6 [latex]\lt[/latex] 7) and runs 3-7 (2 left); P3 (1) runs 7-8; P2 runs 8-10; P4 runs 10-13; P1 runs 13-20.

Turnaround: P1 20, P2 10 [latex]-[/latex] 3 = 7, P3 8 [latex]-[/latex] 7 = 1, P4 13 [latex]-[/latex] 8 = 5.

Average = 33 / 4 = 8.25

Answer: 8.25

questions.text: In which one of the following page replacement algorithms it is possible for the page fault rate to increase even when the number of allocated frames increases?
questions.solution:
This is Belady's anomaly, which happens with FIFO. LRU, OPT and MRU are stack algorithms: with more frames the set of pages in memory only grows, so faults never increase.

Answer: FIFO

questions.text:
Consider the following proposed solution for the critical section problem. There are n processes: [latex]P_{0}...P_{n-1}[/latex] . In the code,function [latex]pmax[/latex] returns an integer not smaller than any of its arguments. For all i, t[i] is initialized to zero.

Which one of the following is TRUE about the above solution?
questions.solution:
This is a bakery-style algorithm: a process enters only after every other process with a smaller (non-zero) ticket has finished, so mutual exclusion holds.

But two processes can pick the same ticket (pmax is not atomic). Then each waits for the other (t[j] [latex]\le[/latex] t[i] holds both ways) [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] deadlock, so progress and bounded waiting also fail.

Answer: At most one process can be in the critical section at any time

questions.text: Consider a computer system with ten physical page frames. The system is provided with an accessse quence [latex](a_{1},a_{2},...,a_{20},a_{1},a_{2},...,a_{20})[/latex], where each [latex]a_{i}[/latex] is a distinct virtual page number. The difference in the number of page faults between the last-in-first-outpage replacement policy and the optimal page replacement policy is ______.
questions.solution:
LIFO: the first pass gives 20 faults; a1-a9 stay in memory and the 10th frame keeps getting replaced (ends with a20). Second pass: a1-a9 hit, a10-a20 fault (11). Total 31.

Optimal: 20 faults in the first pass and only 10 in the second (it keeps 10 of the pages needed next). Total 30.

Difference = 31 [latex]-[/latex] 30 = 1

Answer: 1
